segments.text: Yata hai evam ata shudvidya sarupam uktu yuktivir asaditamapi yata na na shiti tatha sarodashasu
yogina saavdhaneena bavitaviyam.
Now the author here explains that a yogi must be fully aware in each and every state
of life, so that this state of pure knowledge of consciousness remains stable and does not
get subsided in any way.
Saavdhaneena means you should remain fully aware.
Trishu, Chaturtham, Tailavat, Aasai, Jamm, the four-turya state, Chaturtham, the four-turya
state must be expandedly expanded in such a way that it gets its pervajan in all the other
three states, Jagat, Sopranand, Sashivthi, also, in wakefulness, in dreaming state and in dreamless
state, so that in these three states also, that Turya is found, Trishu, Jagaradishu, Padeshu,
in three states means Jagaradishu, Padeshu, in this state, in these Jagat, Sopranand, Sashivthi.
Chaturtham, the fourth, fourth is Shuddha Vidya Prakash Rupam, Turya Nanda Rasaathmakam
Dhamma, which is filled with pure knowledge and pure light, and which is filled with the
ecstasy and joy of Turya. That state must be sprinkled and expanded just like oil,
Tailavat. It means, Yatat-Tailam Kramena, Aadikamadikam Prasadath, Arshem Vyafnodhi, just as
oil sticks and expands on any support, cloth, etc. and retains on it. In this way,
Yogi must expand the state of Turya in all the other three states.
As the state of Turya is in all the three states, at the trim of entry, or at the time
at the moment of entry and at the moment of exit from it. At the time of entering in
Turya and entering in vagueness, dreaming state and dreamless state, or at the time of coming
out from these three states, you find Turya existing. Turya exists at the point of entry
and at the point of exit in these three states, Jagrath Sopranand Sushapati. In the same way,
you must prolong it in such a way that Turya Rasa becomes established in the middle state
of Jagrath Sopranand Sushapati also, not only in the beginning and in the end, not only in
the entry and in the state of exit coming out from Jagrath Sopranand Sushapati. In the center
also, you must see that Turya is pervading in all these three states. It is, he says, Parisuprata,
Turya Haseena, Majdashama-pi, Awashtam-yukhtya. The Yukhtya, the means, just Awashtam, hold it,
hold it at the time of entry, hold it at the time of exit. The Turya Rasa must be held properly in
full awareness so that the Turya Rasa is expanded in the center of all these three states. Yena
Tanma-ibhavam-afnayaat. Hence Yogi becomes one with that Turya Rasa in all these three states.
Jagrath Sopranand Sushapati, Turya Bhoga-Sambhava. This first Sutta also explains in first
awakening seven Sutta. Jagrath Sopranand Sushapati, Turya Bhoga-Sambhava. The state of Turya is found
in Jagrath, in Sopranand Sushapati. This is written in first awakening of Sushutras. By this Sutta,
it is explained that Uddam-Shakti-Chakra-Ano-Sandya-Awashtam-Bbhaja, Saras-Praserat-Jagar-Adi-Pasesh-U,
Sattam-Atram-Turyasi-Uhtam. There he has explained Turya, that Turya is already found in Jagrath,
in Sopna and in Sushapati, in the first awakening of this Sutta. And in the 11th Sutta of
the first awakening is another Sutta, just similar to it, Treti-Bhokta-Virya-Sahaha. The digester of
three is hero. The one who digest all these three states in his own nature, in his own God consciousness,
is hero. If Shambho-Pai-Ano-Guna-Hat-Pai-Yukta-Jagar-Adi-Samharo-Darshita, in this Sutta, it is explained that
by holding the means of Shambho-Pai, with force, Hat-Pai-Yukta-Jagar-Adi-Samharo-Darshita,
he has explained that Jagrath, Sopranand Sushakti, are subsided and subsided just they meld in Turya.
It is, but here, in the Sutta and in this Sutta, Treshu-Choturtham-Tailava-Tasej, this Sutta in on, in
third awakening of Shusutra, Anu, Anu-Chita-Avashtam-Yukta-Dalakal-Pam-Jagar-Adi-Trayam-Turya-Aasiktham-Karium-Yed-Duktham.
Here all those three states are separated from Turya, as Sutta is separated from it is Shat.
You know Shat?
Shat.
In which word is kept?
In the same way, Jagrath-Sopranand Sushakti are found in the Shaita of Turya.
Although being separated, they are united with each other.
In the same manner, Yogi must here be aware that this Jagrath-Sopranand Sushakti are found in one.
